Chunk index: 0

Speech chunk:
Mr. Speaker, it is my honour to present a petition on behalf of a number of residents of the fine City of Calgary, Alberta, as well as residents of Black Creek, Courtenay, Nanaimo, Cumberland, and Comox, British Columbia. While they are different petitions, they deal with the same concern that the federal Government lacks a mandate from the Canadian people to conclude a trade deal with the U.S. They believe that the deal would deny Canada the policy freedom to determine its own economic future and would undermine our ability to develop a society distinct from that of the U.S. Therefore, they ask Parliament to dissolve now to enable the people of Canada an opportunity to accept or reject the proposed trade deal during a national general election.

BasePK: 3735569
Chunk index: 0

Speech chunk:
Mr. Speaker, I would like to explain again the American governmental system. There is a separation between the executive and the legislative branch, and the legislative branch known as Congress does not trust the executive always. The congressional drafting rule is that they do not wish to have any legislation that amends any other legislation unless they know specifically what has been amended. Although the U.S. administration suggested there be a clause in their legislation which would state that any possible inconsistent federal legislation should be overridden by this particular Bill, the congressional committees changed that recommendation back to their traditional practice. I would suggest to the hon. gentleman, after he consults Legal Aid, that he go down and address his objection to the American congressional committees. We simply do not control them.
